lines.text: Every motor on this robot is controlled with requests. A request tells the motor controller what to do right now.
You've already sent a few in Tuner X. Voltage Out pushed the motor with a fixed voltage, and Motion Magic moved it to a position.
And remember how Voltage Out kept running until you stopped it? Our code works the same way.
Here's the code we wrote. The left trigger is bound to a command that sets the arm to six volts.
Press the trigger, and that command sends a six volt request to the motor. The arm climbs.
Now let go. The command ends.
Ending a command doesn't remove its request. Six volts is still on the motor, and nothing has told it to do anything else.
Try it yourself. Hold the trigger, then let go.
So when the trigger is released, we need to stop the motor. We add a second binding that runs the arm's stop command.
That command calls stop motor, a function built into CTRE's motor class. It replaces whatever request is running with neutral, so the motor stops pushing.
Let's try it again. Hold the trigger, and the arm climbs just like before. Now let go.
This time the arm stops pushing and swings back down.
A request stays on the motor until something replaces it. So whenever a command ends, decide what replaces it.
